record.title: The structural conjecture for vertically 4-connected matroids with a modular 4-point line
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a simple, vertically $4$-connected matroid with a modular $4$-point line $L$.

**Structural conjecture.** Either $M$ is ternary, for some $e\in L$ the deletion $M\backslash e$ is binary, or $M$ has an $F_7$-minor and either an $F_7^-$- or $(F_7^-)^*$-minor.

This conjecture proposes that, among simple vertically $4$-connected matroids with a modular $4$-point line, the known ternary case and the case obtained by deleting one element to obtain a binary matroid account for all possibilities apart from the specified $F_7$ and non-Fano minor configuration. The surrounding discussion presents it as a likely classification and does not state that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Rohan Kapadia, “Matroids with a modular 4-point line”, arXiv:1309.5329 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.5329

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

record.title: Erdős's conjecture on odd cycle lengths in triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph with chromatic number $k$, and let $\frac{}{ }$ denote a positive real parameter. **Erdős's conjecture.** For every $\frac{}{ } > 0$, there exists $k_0(\frac{}{ })$ such that, for $k \geq k_0(\frac{}{ })$, every triangle-free $k$-chromatic graph contains more than $k^{2-\frac{}{ }}$ odd cycles of different lengths.

The conjecture concerns how many distinct odd cycle lengths must occur in triangle-free graphs of large chromatic number. The paper proves a stronger result, namely that such graphs contain cycles of a quadratic-logarithmic number of consecutive lengths, so this conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Alexandr Kostochka, Benny Sudakov and Jacques Verstraete, “Cycles in triangle-free graphs of large chromatic number”, arXiv:1404.4544 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.4544

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2014); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The full Erdős–Ko–Rado conjecture for t-intersecting perfect matchings
record.statement:
Let $K_{2n}$ be the complete graph on $2n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of its perfect matchings. The family is **$t$-intersecting** if $|m\cap m'|>t$ for all $m,m'\in\mathcal{F}$. It is **trivially $t$-intersecting** when, for some collection $T$ of $t$ pairwise disjoint 2-sets of $[2n]$, 
$$
\mathcal{F}_T=\{m\in\mathcal{M}_{2n}:T\subseteq m\}.
$$
 **The full Erdős–Ko–Rado conjecture for t-intersecting perfect matchings.** If $\mathcal{F}$ is a $t$-intersecting family of perfect matchings of $K_{2n}$, then 
$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq (2(n-t)-1)!!.
$$
 Moreover, equality holds if and only if $\mathcal{F}$ is trivially $t$-intersecting. This extends the known Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem for intersecting families of perfect matchings and remains an open generalization for $t$-intersecting families.
record.source_name: Nathan Lindzey, “Erdős-Ko-Rado for Perfect Matchings”, arXiv:1409.2057 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.2057

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

record.title: Balogh, Kostochka and Treglown's degree-sequence Hajnal–Szemerédi conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n,r\in\mathbb N$ with $r$ dividing $n$. Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with degree sequence $d_1\leq\dots\leq d_n$. **Balogh, Kostochka and Treglown's conjecture.** If

$$
d_i\geq (r-2)n/r+i
$$

for all $i<n/r$, and

$$
d_{n/r+1}\geq (r-1)n/r,
$$

then $G$ contains a perfect $K_r$-packing. A perfect $K_r$-packing is a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_r$ covering all vertices of $G$. This conjecture proposes a degree-sequence analogue of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem, characterising sufficient degree conditions for a perfect clique packing; its resolution status is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Andrew Treglown, “A degree sequence Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem”, arXiv:1412.1774 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.1774

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

record.title: Erdős–Rubin–Taylor conjecture on scaling choosability parameters
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $(a,b)$-choosability mean that every assignment of lists of size $a$ to the vertices of $G$ admits a coloring in which each vertex receives a color from its list and each color is used on at most $b$ vertices. **Erdős–Rubin–Taylor conjecture.** If $G$ is $(a,b)$-choosable, then $G$ is $(an,bn)$-choosable for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$. A positive answer to part (i) of Problem 1 would follow from this conjecture; its resolution is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Balázs Keszegh and Xuding Zhu, “Choosability and paintability of the lexicographic product of graphs”, arXiv:1502.03977 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03977

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2015).

record.title: Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture on P-recursiveness of pattern-avoidance sequences
record.statement:
Let $S_k$ be the symmetric group on $k$ letters. For a fixed finite set of patterns $\subset S_k$, let $C_n(\mathcal{F})$ be the number of permutations in $S_n$ avoiding every pattern in $\mathcal{F}$. An integer sequence $\{a_n\}$ is **P-recursive** if it satisfies a nontrivial linear recurrence with polynomial coefficients, namely

$$
q_0(n)a_n+q_1(n)a_{n-1}+\cdots+q_k(n)a_{n-k}=0
$$

for some $q_i(x)\in\mathbb Z[x]$. **Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture.** For every fixed finite set of patterns $\mathcal{F}\subset S_k$, the sequence $\{C_n(\mathcal{F})\}$ is P-recursive. This was a longstanding conjecture supported by many positive results for special pattern sets, but the paper disproves it.
record.source_name: Scott Garrabrant and Igor Pak, “Pattern avoidance is not P-recursive”, arXiv:1505.06508 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.06508

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2015). “The Noonan--Zeilberger conjecture is false.”

record.title: Ingleton's critical-graph excluded-minor conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be a critical graph with no obstructions, and let $M(\Delta)$ be the matroid whose lattice of cyclic flats is $\mathcal{Z}_\Delta$.

**Ingleton's critical-graph conjecture.** If $\Delta$ is a critical graph with no obstructions, then $M(\Delta)$ is an excluded minor for $\mathcal{BO}$.

This reformulates a conjecture attributed to Ingleton. The paper proves a special case, while the assertion for all critical graphs with no obstructions remains open.
record.source_name: Joseph E. Bonin and Thomas J. Savitsky, “An infinite family of excluded minors for strong base-orderability”, arXiv:1507.05521 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.05521

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

record.title: The algebraic Erdős–Ko–Rado conjecture for finite 2-transitive groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite $2$-transitive group. For each coset of a point stabiliser in $G$, let its characteristic vector be the corresponding element of the group algebra $\mathbb{C}G$, and let $V$ be the subspace spanned by these characteristic vectors. If $S$ is an intersecting set of maximal cardinality in $G$, write $\chi_S$ for its characteristic vector. **Algebraic Erdős–Ko–Rado conjecture.** Then

$$
\chi_S\in V.
$$

This conjecture proposes an algebraic analogue of the Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem. The paper proves the assertion for some $2$-transitive groups, but its validity for arbitrary finite $2$-transitive groups remains open.
record.source_name: Karen Meagher, Pablo Spiga and Pham Huu Tiep, “An Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem for finite 2-transitive groups”, arXiv:1507.06450 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.06450

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

record.title: Weak convergence for rooted graphs excluding a finite set of minors
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite set of finite connected graphs, and let $Ex^{\bullet}(\mathcal S)$ be the class of rooted, labelled or unlabelled, connected graphs with no minor in $\mathcal S$. Let $R_n$ be a uniformly random element of $Ex^{\bullet}(\mathcal S)$ with $n$ vertices.

**Rooted minor-exclusion convergence conjecture.** The sequence $R_n$ converges weakly.

This is an early formulation of the paper's main question. The paper proves the analogous convergence for important special cases, including subcritical classes, while the general minor-closed case remains open in this formulation.
record.source_name: Agelos Georgakopoulos and Stephan Wagner, “Limits of subcritical random graphs and random graphs with excluded minors”, arXiv:1512.03572 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03572

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: Benjamini--Schramm convergence for graphs excluding a finite set of minors
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite set of finite connected graphs, and let $Ex(\mathcal S)$ be the class of labelled or unlabelled connected graphs with no minor in $\mathcal S$. Let $G_n$ be a uniformly random element of $Ex(\mathcal S)$ with $n$ vertices.

**Minor-exclusion Benjamini--Schramm conjecture.** The sequence $G_n$ Benjamini--Schramm converges.

The conjecture is the unrooted counterpart of the rooted weak-convergence question. The paper proves it for several subcritical families, but the general minor-closed case is not established here.
record.source_name: Agelos Georgakopoulos and Stephan Wagner, “Limits of subcritical random graphs and random graphs with excluded minors”, arXiv:1512.03572 (2016).

record.title: Equality in the generalised Ramsey number lower bound
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{C}$ be the set of all pairs of non-empty sets of cycles, and let $R(\Ga_1,\Ga_2)$ be the corresponding generalised Ramsey number. For $(\Ga_1,\Ga_2)\in\mathfrak{C}$, let $\mathfrak{m}(\Ga_1,\Ga_2)$ be the number defined by

$$
\mathfrak{m}(\Ga_1,\Ga_2)=\max\!\big(5,\min(\ga^2+\ga_e^1/2-1,2\ga^2-1),\min(\ga^1+\ga_e^2/2-1,2\ga^1-1)\big).
$$

Theorem~ gives the lower bound $R(\Ga_1,\Ga_2)\geq \mathfrak{m}(\Ga_1,\Ga_2)$, with the stronger bound $R(\Ga_1,\Ga_2)\geq \mathfrak{m}(\Ga_1,\Ga_2)+1$ for the exceptional class specified there. **Equality conjecture.** Equality holds in the lower bound of Theorem~ for all pairs $(\Ga_1,\Ga_2)\in\mathfrak{C}$.

The conjecture extends the cases established in the theorem, including all pairs for which $\min(\Ga_1\cup\Ga_2)\leq 6$ and the specified classes $\mathfrak{C}_1\cup\mathfrak{C}_2$, as well as the special case where both shortest-cycle lengths are even. Determining whether equality always holds remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Mikael Hansson, “Generalised Ramsey numbers for two sets of cycles”, arXiv:1605.04301 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.04301

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

record.title: Thomassen's finiteness conjecture for 5-list-critical graphs on surfaces
record.statement: Let $d4a2$ be a surface, and let $G$ be a graph embedded in $d4a2$. A list assignment $L$ assigns a set of colors to each vertex; $G$ is **$L$-critical** if it has no $L$-coloring but every proper subgraph of $G$ has an $L$-coloring. **Thomassen's conjecture.** For every surface $d4a2$ there are, up to isomorphism, only finitely many graphs $G$ such that $G$ embeds in $d4a2$ and is $L$-critical for some $5$-list assignment $L$. This asks for a finite obstruction set for $5$-list-colorability on each fixed surface; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Luke Postle and Robin Thomas, “Hyperbolic families and coloring graphs on surfaces”, arXiv:1609.06749 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.06749

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2016).

record.title: Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $A,B$ be non-empty subsets of $\mathbb{F}_p$. For subsets $A,B\subset\mathbb{F}_p$, write $A+B=\{a+b\mid a\in A,\ b\in B\}$ and define the **restricted sumset** $A\dot{+}B=\{a+b\mid a\in A,\ b\in B,\ a\neq b\}$. **Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture.** For every $A\subset\mathbb{F}_p$, 

$$
|A\dot{+}A|\geqslant\min\left\{p,2|A|-3\right\}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the restricted analogue of the Cauchy–Davenport theorem and was later proved, so the database status is recorded as solved.
record.source_name: Eric Balandraud, “Addition Theorems in Fp via the Polynomial Method”, arXiv:1702.06419 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.06419

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Brown–Graham–Landman 2-large conjecture
record.statement: Let $D\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^+$, and let $r\in\mathbb{Z}^+$. An arithmetic progression $a,a+d,a+2d,\dots,a+(k-1)d$ with $d\in D$ is a **$D$-arithmetic progression** (or $D$-ap). The set $D$ is **$r$-large** if, for every $k\in\mathbb{Z}^+$, every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{Z}^+$ admits a monochromatic $k$-term $D$-ap; it is **large** if it is $r$-large for every $r\in\mathbb{Z}^+$. **2-large conjecture.** If $D$ is $2$-large, then $D$ is large. This conjecture asks whether the existence of arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $D$ for every two-coloring already implies the corresponding property for every finite number of colors. The source attributes it to Brown, Graham, and Landman; its resolution is not given here.
record.source_name: Aaron Robertson, “Down the Large Rabbit Hole”, arXiv:1709.07303 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.07303

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2017).

record.title: Asymmetric density criterion for Ramsey-infinite ordered graph pairs
record.statement:
Let $H$ and $H'$ be ordered graphs with asymmetric $2$-density parameters satisfying $m_2(H)\geq m_2(H')$. Let $m(F)$ denote the relevant density of a graph $F$, and let $R_<(H,H')$ be the family of Ramsey graphs of $(H,H')$. **Asymmetric density conjecture.** If

$$
m(F)>m_2(H,H')
$$

for every $F\in R_<(H,H')$, then $(H,H')$ is Ramsey infinite. This is proposed as an asymmetric extension of the paper's symmetric density result; the cited random-Ramsey results provide partial motivation, while the ordered statement remains open.
record.source_name: Jonathan Rollin, “Minimal Ordered Ramsey Graphs”, arXiv:1712.09034 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09034

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2017). “In the ordered setting several cases remain open, even if Conjectures and hold.”

record.title: The list $Delta$-Equitable Coloring Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected finite simple graph. A list assignment $L$ assigns a list of colors to each vertex; it is a $k$-assignment when $|L(v)|=k$ for every $v\in V(G)$. An equitable $L$-coloring is a proper coloring using colors from the lists such that each color appears on at most $\lceil |V(G)|/k\rceil$ vertices. The graph is equitably $k$-choosable when it has an equitable $L$-coloring for every $k$-assignment $L$. Let $K_m$, $C_{2m+1}$, and $K_{2m+1,2m+1}$ denote respectively a complete graph, an odd cycle, and a complete bipartite graph with parts of size $2m+1$.

**List $\Delta$-ECC.** $G$ is equitably $k$-choosable for each $k\geq\Delta(G)$ if it is different from $K_m$, $C_{2m+1}$, and $K_{2m+1,2m+1}$.

This is the list-context analogue of the $Delta$-Equitable Coloring Conjecture. The source presents it as a conjecture attributed to KP03, but gives no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Hemanshu Kaul, Jeffrey A. Mudrock, Michael J. Pelsmajer and Benjamin Reiniger, “Proportional Choosability: A New List Analogue of Equitable Coloring”, arXiv:1806.06966 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.06966

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

record.title: Las Vergnas's second Tutte polynomial conjecture for binary matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a binary matroid, let $T_M(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial, and let $z$ be an integer. **Las Vergnas's second conjecture.** The value

$$
\frac{T_M(-1+4z,-1+4z)}{T_M(-1,-1)}
$$

is an odd integer for every binary matroid $M$ and every integer $z$. This conjecture is the second of three conjectures made by Michel Las Vergnas concerning evaluations of the Tutte polynomial of binary matroids; it is stronger than the first conjecture and weaker than the third. The first conjecture was proved, while the third was disproved; this second conjecture is presented here as the subject of counterexamples.
record.source_name: Robert Brijder and Hendrik Jan Hoogeboom, “Counterexamples to a conjecture of Las Vergnas”, arXiv:1809.00813 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.00813

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2018); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Strictly balanced factors are as informative as unbalanced factors
record.statement:
Let $\Sigma=\{\mathtt{a},\mathtt{b}\}$, and let $\Sigma_{sb}^{n}$ denote the strictly balanced words of length $n$. For a word $w$, write $\operatorname{ScatFact}_k(w)$ for its set of length-$k$ scattered factors. Two words are reconstructed from their $k$-spectra when equality of the relevant scattered-factor sets forces the words to be equal. **Strictly balanced reconstruction conjecture.** For strictly balanced words $w$, the strictly balanced scattered factors are just as informative as the unbalanced scattered factors: for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, if $k'=k+1$ for odd $k$ and $k'=k+2$ for even $k$, and $w,w'\in\Sigma_{sb}^{2k}$ satisfy

$$
\operatorname{ScatFact}_{k'}(w)\cap\Sigma_{sb}^{k'}=\operatorname{ScatFact}_{k'}(w')\cap\Sigma_{sb}^{k'},
$$

then $w=w'$. This conjecture concerns reconstruction of strictly balanced binary words from their strictly balanced scattered factors; the source states that it is unresolved, while proving it for words with at most two blocks of $[?]$-letters and, by symmetry, at most two blocks of the other letter.
record.source_name: Joel D. Day, Pamela Fleischmann, Florin Manea and Dirk Nowotka, “k-Spectra of weakly-c-Balanced Words”, arXiv:1904.09125 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.09125

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2019). “While we do not resolve the conjecture, we give an example of a subclass of words for which it holds true, namely when there are at most two ‘blocks’ of $\tb$’s (and therefore by symmetry if there are at most two ‘blocks’ of $\ta$’s).”

record.title: Infinite Gallai theorem for vertex-disjoint T-paths
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a possibly infinite graph and let $T\subseteq V$. A system $\mathcal{P}$ of vertex-disjoint $T$-paths and a set $X\subseteq V$ are required to satisfy: for every component $Y$ of $G-X$, the paths contained in $Y$ cover all but at most one vertex of $T\cap Y$, and $X\subseteq V(\mathcal{P})$ with $|V(P)\cap X|\leq 1$ for every $P\in\mathcal{P}$.

**Gallai's conjecture.** There exists such a system $\mathcal{P}$ and set $X$.

This is proposed as an infinite generalization of Gallai's theorem; the supplied text does not state that it has been proved.
record.source_name: Attila Joó, “The Lovász-Cherkassky theorem in countable graphs”, arXiv:2102.04203 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.04203

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

record.title: Clique-minor separating-pair conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$. **Clique-minor separating-pair conjecture.** There exist non-isomorphic graphs $H$ and $H'$ such that

$$
\hom(F,H)\ne\hom(F,H')\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F\text{ contains }K_n\text{ as a minor}.
$$

Here $K_n$ is the complete graph on $n$ vertices. The paper says that proving this conjecture for every $n$ would suffice to prove the non-isomorphism conjecture for proper minor- and union-closed families; it is left open.
record.source_name: David E. Roberson, “Oddomorphisms and homomorphism indistinguishability over graphs of bounded degree”, arXiv:2206.10321 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.10321

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).
